Immediate optimistic outcome; no server write before validation accepts.
Rejected action restores exact checkpoint and cancels dependent actions.
A new editor never reuses a prior value or confirmation flag.
Delayed close events cannot clear or close a newer editor.
Sync Off preserves microphone visibility and recognition.
One utterance cannot execute both a short command and its preempting continuation.
Returning from Trip Log preserves underlying editor value and surface.
Ready / End Trip uses one immutable timestamp for end/start boundary.
End <break type> OK skips question and dialog; standalone final End <break type> shows both.
Scheduled Start accepts a valid duration with or without the Standard Time prefix.
Break Selector is pointer-only; voice start commands use a typed OK/Cancel dialog.
Localized command patterns dispatch neutral interval identifiers; core logic does not parse English break names.
Only the End command matching the active semantic interval type is eligible.
Recognition off/sleep while voice editing switches to keypad and preserves value.
Trip summary stays until OK/Cancel; no automatic editor open.
A spoken range command announces Viewing once and suppresses mode feedback.
Every suppressed component identifies its rule and suppressing owner; optional is not the same as skippable.

Specify settings draft/save/cancel behavior per settings section, including focus return and validation errors.
Attach automated and production-version evidence to every transition; keep unverified paths gray.
Confirm preferred mode grouping and state names.
Approve the proposed presentation priority tiers; eligibility is dynamic, not a single fixed numeric rank.
Review conditional Lunch question and automatic late-break restart branches.
Confirm whether authentication/settings/training should be added beyond mainline scope.

Recognition is the existing orthogonal speechRecognition attribute. Method pin/password selects credential UI. Voice and User[name] are local switches, including clearing loopbacks. Busy login blocks switches. Shared state actions loginInput/loginDigits/loginPassword/loginSwitch drive both buttons and speech availability. cancelPrimed distinguishes first/second PIN Cancel; credentials remain private. Default User view mirrors the exact time and percentage components from publisher uiState.
Watcher percentage, Sync, mode and time-display overrides are client-only; Use user’s settings clears overrides.
Display user Trip goal, mode goal, selected effective Auto scope, and Sync on/off from the same publisher uiState.
Never expose Start Break, Down or End Trip actions in the observer.
Reuse one observer ClockTimer and reload its read-only model on user switch; it cannot tick lifecycle transitions or write persistence.
Closed open-ended intervals export an explicit interval.ended event; after Down Time ends the observer returns to running without pending latency.
Repeated snapshots with unchanged incoming timer events update time, totals and viewer settings without replaying intervals or replacing their dial renderers.
Authorized snapshots whitelist active timer events, display attributes and aggregates; exclude credentials, queued trips and pending writes.
Previous/Next and recent-user selection stop the old connection before opening the new authorized peer. Clear stale readouts and unsent messages; restore that user’s local preferences.
Trainer messages target the current watched user and are disabled during switching.
Down Time displays elapsed count-up; Lunch and breaks display remaining count-down then overtime count-up. These follow the publisher interval independently of viewer goals, Sync and mode.
The compact mirror shows the watched name and omits Trip Log and all lifecycle action buttons.
Drop-In is a standalone page at drop-in.php, opened in a separate tab; main app keeps publishing. Viewer loads no speech recognizer, app.js or trip lifecycle controls.
Reuse the existing authenticated session; unauthorized users cannot watch or send messages. Account Lookup retains its separate permission check.

contracts.login: Main page authenticates an admin-assigned four-digit login ID and four-digit PIN. Database primary user ID remains distinct. PIN stored as bcrypt hash. Main-page connect-pin validates exact ASCII digits and leading zeros; other pages retain connect username/password. Failed match retains ID and returns to empty PIN entry. Server enforces per-ID and per-origin limits. Admin assignment requires modify-users permission and target access. English Voice selects four-digit login; User or Username (including User name) selects legacy login. Both commands clear all inputs and repeat the destination prompt, including same-mode loopbacks. Tiny pointer buttons switch modes. Recognition state is preserved; speech requires listening.
contracts.login-input: ID prompt Please login using voice; four digits and OK enter PIN stage, announcing Password. Cancel in either stage clears both and repeats ID prompt. PIN cells render *. On success English speech is Login successful, say standard time or ready at. Off/sleep preserves stage and digits; pointer entry remains available. Wake/on resumes the same stage. English vocabulary and messages are selected-language resources. Recognition status and enable/wake control are visible in both login methods. Only listening exposes login voice commands; pointer/keyboard controls remain available unless login is pending. Recognition lifecycle and local digit/method commands bypass the persistence queue. Rejected pending switches return immediately. Recognition events do not replay login prompts; existing recognition feedback owns its announcement. Username/password is a separate legacy modal; only one login modal is open. First PIN Cancel clears only PIN and repeats Password; the second clears ID too. Voice restarts ID entry. Both modals are centered in the visual viewport above the visible mic/options safe top, constrain their height, and scroll internally on short screens. Boundary recalculates on mic/options changes and visual viewport resize/scroll. A fresh four-digit sequence replaces the selected ID/PIN; consecutive complete groups keep the latest group, including an eight-digit utterance. First PIN Cancel clears PIN and primes a second Cancel; the second clears both credentials and returns to ID. New entry, confirmation, or switching methods resets this sequence. Cancel Cancel works in one utterance. Recognition changes preserve it. Rejected PIN login clears only PIN, resets cancelPrimed, retains User ID, announces Login failed. Password, and permits retry. Login via voice from the legacy modal waits there with voiceRequested=true until the model is ready, then transfers automatically.
contracts.startup: At launch queue Application is loading; the startup dialog OK button initializes audio and releases it exactly once. No automatic startup speech before user activation. Four-digit login UI can accept pointer input while the recognition model loads. Voice login commands are unavailable in speechRecognition=starting. Defer the voice ID/PIN prompt until SpeechMenu.modelReady after recognizer, VAD and audio capture initialization; release only the latest prompt for the current login modal. UI and recognition initialization continue while startup playback is pending; unsupported speech releases the barrier immediately. Only the latest prompt for the still-open current modal is released. Startup focus is STARTUP-AUDIO, with a single OK button usable by pointer or keyboard; other dialog openings wait for activation. Do not show success, populate a newly authenticated profile, or close the modal until the server accepts credentials. Login uses explicit request/response handling and does not enter optimistic trip-persistence transactions. Rejected PIN login retains ID, clears PIN/cancelPrimed, stays on PIN, and announces Login failed. Password.

No match renders an error and clears the editor. Autogenerated account ID is readonly and excluded from writes; names, preferred name, username, replacement password, four-digit login ID, replacement PIN and permissions are editable subject to server authorization. Existing password/PIN are never returned or populated. Empty replacement secrets retain credentials; initial voice credentials require ID and PIN together, later independent edits preserve the other credential. Loading and saving disable editing; success is shown only after server confirmation. Rejected saves retain editable non-secret input and show the server error. New utterances may capture immediately; requested final results for earlier accepted commands remain routable until completion or explicit cancellation.
Cancellation and rollback settle once, including all dependent actions, after cooperating or late callbacks have finished.
Applying must describe a tracked executing/validating/committing operation, never a discarded callback. Recognition awaiting-result is a separate lifecycle phase.
Login remains non-optimistic and outside the state-changing command pipeline.
async-operation-lifecycle.known_test_baseline: The loopback-only fixture fails on trip mode in both current production source and isolated prototype. This is not evidence that all suites pass.
async-operation-lifecycle.validation_and_retry: Validation work remains tracked in the transaction. Retry status and attempts are exposed separately. Phase-specific UI wording and exhaustive state invariant enforcement are deferred.

state-validity.status: Initial explicit mainline validity rules; not yet exhaustive or runtime-enforced. Existing unresolved transition guards remain unresolved.
state-validity.model: Visible state = focus plus trip attributes plus orthogonal recognition, configuration and operation lifecycle regions. Node identity alone is not a validity check.
global: An active break/lunch/down interval requires an active trip.
Voicepad must not remain open when recognition is off or sleeping; transition automatically to numberpad. Temporary suspension for playback is distinct from disabling recognition.
Confirmation requires a valid current value; an empty editor cannot confirm.
An optimistic active trip may temporarily lack its permanent ID only while an owned validated start operation is pending.
A rejected operation restores its prior valid state and cancels dependent operations.
No pending operation may exist without an owner, outstanding result/work, or an explicit retry condition.
unresolved: Scheduled draft timing/duration validity needs an explicit draft attribute in the global state.
Exact availability and authorization for each transition need executable predicates from the shared state, not prose placeholders.
Clock phase and Auto goal/range combinations require a full cross-region validity audit.
Drop-In connection validity must be checked independently of watched trip state and local viewer overrides.
